text.p: Analysts welcomed the purchase of Kaposplast Kft by Hungarian plastics group Pannonplast Rt, but they said the acquisition will only benefit the company from next year.
"The expansion is positive news," said Balint Hada of New York Broker Budapest. "It's probable that they chose one of the best opportunities in Hungary."
Pannonplast announced on Friday the full acquisition of Kaposplast, a plastics processing company producing mainly fasteners and binding materials for packaging.
Following the announcement Pannonplast shares hit a new high of 4,720 forints on Friday which they extended once again to a new record of 4,900 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday.
Analysts said the acquisition will substantially boost Pannonplast group's sales from next year.
"Pannonplast will consolidate (Kaposplast's results) only for the last quarter of 1996, so we expect the real benefit from Kaposplast to come in 1997," said Eva Kormendi of Concorde Securities.
Hada said Kaposplast's products fit into Pannonplast's profile, although some refurbishment needs to be done before the new purchase bears fruit.
"The acquisition won't mean an immediate increase in Pannonplast's profits," he said, referring to Pannonplast's statement that new investments and development projects in Kaposplast were imminent.
Pannonplast also announced on Friday that a Romanian court had registered a new subsidiary in Cluj owned by Pannonpipe Kft -- a group unit 50 percent-owned by Pannonplast.
Kormendi said that Concorde expects Kaposplast and the new Romanian plant to boost group sales in 1997 by almost one billion forints over the 1996 estimated figure of around 10 billion forints.
Analysts expressed little surprise at the Kaposplast purchase as the market had expected some kind of acquisition following the group's recent capital increase.
Kaposplast's sales in 1995 reached 656 million forints, with 40 percent of this exported, while its operating profit was 40 million.
